title: SentinelIQ
summary: Predictive maintenance automation combining TCN-LSTM forecasting, dual anomaly detection, SHAP attribution, and PuLP scheduling.
problem: Maintenance planning benefits from forecast, anomaly, and explanation signals in one operational flow.
solution: An automated pipeline connecting sequence models, dual anomaly detection (Isolation Forest + Autoencoder), SHAP attribution, and PuLP intervention scheduling.
architecture: Case-study context: Maintenance planning benefits from one operational path that combines remaining-useful-life signals, anomaly detection, explanations, and scheduling instead of leaving each result in a separate notebook.
Sequence prediction: Sensor histories move through TCN/LSTM sequence models for remaining-useful-life estimation. Components: PyTorch, TCN, LSTM.
Anomaly and explanation layer: Two anomaly approaches and SHAP attribution expose unusual behavior and the signals behind a prediction. Components: Isolation Forest, Autoencoder, SHAP.

Decision surface: PuLP turns model and anomaly outputs into a planning step, with FastAPI and the web application providing the delivery surface. Components: PuLP, FastAPI, Next.js 15, PostgreSQL, Docker.
Sensor histories feed TCN/LSTM sequence models for remaining-useful-life estimation.
Isolation Forest and an Autoencoder provide two anomaly signals; SHAP attribution exposes contributing signals.
PuLP turns prediction and anomaly outputs into an intervention-planning step, delivered through FastAPI and a Next.js 15/PostgreSQL application.
The repository README documents Docker and local-development routes; the portfolio does not make a winning-model performance claim.
outcomes: NASA CMAPSS RUL study with anomaly detection, SHAP attribution, and scheduling.
Separated prediction, anomaly, explainability, and scheduling responsibilities.
